# opentags

> opentags makes simple ultra-wideband (UWB) hardware for real-time ranging and positioning development in robotics. The product, opentag one, is a compact UWB tag (STM32 + Qorvo DWM3000 radio, Rust/Embassy firmware, USB-C, CAN FD hardware, 6–24V input) for work where GPS will not reach. Designed and assembled in San Diego, CA.

Key facts:

- Product: opentag one, a UWB distance and indoor location tag in a PETG enclosure with clear lid
- Kits: Distance kit (2 tags, $199) gives live point-to-point distance; Location kit (5 tags, $499) provides indoor location hardware with 4 fixed anchors plus 1 mobile tag
- Engineering targets pending ground-truthed validation: ±10 cm TWR ranging accuracy, ±20 cm TDOA position accuracy, 50 Hz update rate, 60 m line-of-sight range
- Preliminary TWR evidence from one pair and the original 50 Hz profile: P95 absolute error was 28.0 mm at the 1 m calibration point, 77.9 mm at 3 m, and 77.3 mm at 5 m; these short indoor line-of-sight runs are not a finished benchmark
- Interfaces: USB-C serial stream, CAN and CAN FD; powered over USB-C or a 6–24V input with reverse-polarity protection
- MCU: STM32 Cortex-M4 at 170 MHz, 256K flash, 128K RAM; radio: Qorvo DWM3000
- Firmware: Rust (Embassy framework); prebuilt roles can be flashed and their serial output monitored in the browser via WebUSB / Web Serial, with no local toolchain. Building the current firmware requires a supplied source checkout; no current public source release is linked.
- Available files: mechanical CAD (STEP) for the full assembly, case, and lid; prebuilt role binaries; Python distance tools; ROS 2 driver and message source packages under Apache-2.0. Current schematics/PCB files are not published.
- Use cases: indoor robot navigation, drone flight without a motion-capture rig, docking and follow-me between machines, UWB anchor network bring-up, asset-tracking prototypes, RF field testing
- Integration: parse live TWR distance and TDOA position from USB serial; ROS 2 publishes range, position, events, and diagnostics
- Availability: ships in about 1 week from San Diego, CA, USA
- Policies: 30-day returns, 1-year limited warranty; sold as a development kit for evaluation (not certified as a finished consumer product)
- Contact: hello@open-tags.com

- [Quickstart](https://open-tags.com/docs/quickstart/): browser-based flashing, connection, calibration, and static testing
- [Location quickstart](https://open-tags.com/docs/location/): anchor survey, 2D/3D configuration, flashing, calibration, and validation limitations
- [Host scripts](https://open-tags.com/docs/scripts/): runnable Python and shell tools for discovery, info, monitoring, calibration, testing, and DFU flashing
- [ROS 2 driver](https://open-tags.com/docs/ros2/): public source download, Jazzy build instructions, topics, services, and validation status
- [ROS 2 source ZIP](https://open-tags.com/docs/ros2/opentags-ros2.zip): driver, message definitions, launch file, configuration, tests, and Apache-2.0 license
- [ROS 2 source on GitHub](https://github.com/open-tags/open-tags.github.io/tree/main/ros2): the source included in the download
- [Range over CAN](https://open-tags.com/docs/can/): optional 500 kbit/s Distance responder bench image, protocol v1, persistent node IDs, Python reader, and DBC; physical-bus validation pending and standard console firmware unchanged
- [Serial protocol](https://open-tags.com/docs/protocol/): commands, responses, distance records, and integration examples
- [Validation](https://open-tags.com/validation/): current benchmark status, engineering targets, and reproducible test protocol
- [Firmware console](https://open-tags.com/firmware/): flash firmware, log data, plot live distance, and calibrate from the browser over WebUSB / Web Serial
- [Privacy](https://open-tags.com/privacy/): website and order privacy policy
- [Terms](https://open-tags.com/terms/): product, ordering, returns, and warranty terms
- [Website source](https://github.com/open-tags/open-tags.github.io): public documentation, distributed binaries, host tools, ROS 2 packages, and the Missing things checklist

## Glossary

- TWR (two-way ranging): one tag pings, the other replies; distance is computed from round-trip time
- TDOA (time-difference of arrival): one mobile tag pings, multiple fixed anchors listen; 3D position is computed from arrival-time deltas
- UWB (ultra-wideband): short-pulse radio that timestamps signal arrival precisely, making it far more accurate for positioning than Bluetooth or Wi-Fi signal strength
